purpose: Test whether a frozen past-volatility scale can turn V6's common-width return interval into stock-specific Top10 intervals and improve the reliability of an abstaining Top3 policy.

preregisteredHypothesis.economicRationale: V6 applied one additive residual interval to every stock in a fold, so lower-bound ordering was identical to point-forecast ordering. Under diffusion scaling, ten-session forecast error should increase with recent daily stock volatility. Normalizing calibration residuals by a frozen sqrt(10)-scaled 20-day volatility may distinguish high expected return with tolerable uncertainty from high expected return caused by volatile names.

knownLimitations: V7 was designed after observing V6, so it is a new counted trial on already contaminated validation and shadow windows.
Recent realized volatility is only a scale proxy; it does not solve V6's unstable point-forecast center or guarantee positive returns.
Sqrt-time diffusion scaling can be wrong during jumps, limit events, volatility clustering and regime changes.
The A-share research panel still uses raw unadjusted prices and has incomplete historical delisting/ST metadata.
Historical success cannot promote V7; only a separately frozen forward shadow cohort could justify another paper-only proposal.
